title: One demo video grew Dropbox's waiting list 15 times
summary: Dropbox posted a three-minute demo video on Digg. Within 24 hours it had more than 10,000 Diggs, and the beta waiting list went from 5,000 to 75,000 people overnight, according to the founder.

beats.say: One three minute video grew a waiting list fifteen times overnight.
The team recorded a short demo of how Dropbox was meant to work.
beats.cap: A demo of how it works

beats.say: It ran about three minutes, and the founder narrated it himself.
The team posted it on Digg, where early tech adopters gathered.
The video was packed with Easter eggs aimed at that crowd.
Within a day, it had more than ten thousand Diggs.
The founder later said it drove hundreds of thousands of people to the site.
And the beta waiting list went from five thousand to seventy five thousand overnight.
A deadpan screen demo drew a crowd.
One short demo video filled the beta waiting list.
beats.cap: One demo. A full waiting list.

claims.note: TechCrunch: within 24 hours the video had more than 10,000 Diggs (the founder's talk says about 12,000)
TechCrunch: more than 10,000 Diggs within 24 hours
TechCrunch: Houston said the beta waiting list grew from 5,000 people to 75,000 'literally overnight'
Stanford talk transcript: Houston says it 'went from 5,000 to 75,000 people overnight'

facts.claim: Dropbox's demo video was about three minutes long and the founder narrated it himself
facts.note: TechCrunch: 'a simple three-minute demonstration'; Drew Houston narrates it personally while the viewer watches his screen

facts.claim: The video was posted on Digg and was full of Easter eggs aimed at the Digg audience
facts.note: TechCrunch: about a dozen Easter eggs aimed at the Digg audience; Stanford transcript: 'we put this video of Dropbox on Digg' (he says March 2008); Hacker News is not mentioned in either source

facts.claim: Within 24 hours the video had more than 10,000 Diggs and drove hundreds of thousands of people to the website
facts.note: TechCrunch: more than 10,000 Diggs in 24 hours; Houston said it 'drove hundreds of thousands of people to the website'

facts.claim: The beta waiting list went from 5,000 to 75,000 people overnight, per the founder
facts.note: Stanford transcript: 'went from 5,000 to 75,000 people overnight'; TechCrunch repeats Houston's figures

facts.claim: The founder described the video as a deadpan demo of him talking over a screen
facts.note: Stanford transcript: 'just this deadpan demo of me talking over a sort of a screen'

youtube.hook: Dropbox posted a roughly three-minute demo video on Digg. Within 24 hours it had more than 10,000 Diggs, and, according to the founder, the beta waiting list went from 5,000 to 75,000 people overnight.
